universities.name: \. KTH Royal Institute of Technology
universities.location: \. KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden
universities.desc: KTH offers a two-year **Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering** taught in English. Students can specialize in Aeronautics, Space, Lightweight Structures or Systems Engineering. The programme includes aerospace modelling, analysis, design and a major engineering project. **Location:** Stockholm, Sweden **![][image1]**

universities.name: \. Chalmers University of Technology
universities.desc: Chalmers offers the related **MSc in NewSpace Systems Engineering**, a two-year programme focusing on space systems, spacecraft design, propulsion, space structures and materials. It is worth considering for students interested in the space technology side of aerospace engineering. **Location:** Gothenburg, Sweden **![][image2]** **Important Note:** KTH is the most directly relevant option for students seeking a master's degree specifically titled Aerospace Engineering. Chalmers' NewSpace Systems Engineering is a related space systems programme, not a degree with the same Aerospace Engineering title. Students researching the **Best Universities for Aerospace Engineering in Sweden** should verify the exact degree title, curriculum, admission requirements and programme availability before applying.

items.q: Can Indian students apply for Aerospace Engineering (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, Indian students with qualifying credentials meeting English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) and academic prerequisites can apply to recognized universities in Sweden.

items.q: What is the medium of instruction for Aerospace Engineering (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Most master's and international bachelor's degree programmes are taught entirely in English for international students across Swedish universities.

items.q: What are the typical tuition fees for Aerospace Engineering (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Tuition fees for international students generally range between SEK 80,000 and SEK 150,000 per year, depending on the institution and level of study.

items.q: Can international students work while studying in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, non-EU international students holding a valid Swedish residence permit for higher education are permitted to work alongside their studies without a fixed hours limitation during term time.
